text: Chapters 1 through 7 gave you every piece of a real enterprise integration — patterns, REST Messages, authentication, exposing data, IntegrationHub, error handling, and MID Servers. This capstone spends four lessons putting all seven chapters together into one real integration: syncing new hires from Meridian HR into ServiceNow.

HR Operations wants new hires created in Meridian HR, their cloud HR system, to automatically produce ServiceNow records before day one. Turning that into a requirements doc means writing down the trigger, the data needed, the target records, the volume, and critically, the source of truth — Meridian HR, never the message that notifies ServiceNow.

Meridian HR's webhook carries a thin payload — just an employee ID, an event type, and a timestamp. It is deliberately not the full employee record, because trusting a notification's contents as if they were authoritative would make ServiceNow's picture of a new hire only as good as whatever happened to be in one HTTP call.

Chapter 1's polling-versus-event-driven distinction decides this integration's shape. Polling would waste calls and delay same-day tasks. Because Meridian HR can initiate contact itself, this is event-driven and inbound — Meridian calls ServiceNow the instant a new hire exists, and ServiceNow responds by pulling the authoritative record back out through a REST Message.

This is the shape of the Scripted REST API resource Lesson 27 builds to receive that webhook. It reads the incoming employeeId off the request body and logs that the notification arrived — a lightweight entry point, not the data pull itself. The real work of pulling the full record happens next, in Lesson 27's REST Message.

Chapter 7 built MID Servers to reach systems with no public endpoint — on-premises databases, legacy apps behind a firewall. Meridian HR is a cloud SaaS with a public HTTPS API, reachable the same way every REST Message since Lesson 4 has been. No MID Server is needed here; an on-prem HR system would flip that decision.

Lesson 27 builds the real authentication and the REST Message this design depends on: an OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials profile, and a RESTMessageV2 call that pulls the full new-hire record straight from Meridian HR's own API.
